messages:
emma: Hey team — customers reporting burst of 502/504s hitting /v1/generate (hosted). Started ~15:02 UTC, affects multiple tenants. Any quick checks?
raj: Looking at traces, gateway shows upstream memcached prefix cache timeouts and `connect` errors. API gateway looping on cache fallback, then timing out to model.
kai: Can you paste a snippet of the gateway logs?
emma: Paste: ```
[15:03:11] gateway: upstream cache error: memcached_auth: AUTH failed (ERR) host=10.12.3.4:11211
[15:03:11] gateway: cache fetch timeout (200ms) key=prefix:customer-1234:prompt
[15:03:13] gateway: falling back to model pool, request latency accumulates -> 504
```
marta: I see a spike in memcached connection resets/timeouts in metrics around 15:01-15:05. Auth failures too. Could be credential rotation or healthcheck flapping.
oncall-sre: I already flipped on `cache.read_timeout_ms` to 500ms to reduce wait time, but still seeing 504s because model nodes get saturated during fallback.
raj: Repro steps I used: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw1","input":"hi"}'` returns 504 intermittently. Gateway logs show: ```
upstream error: memcached CONNECT ECONNRESET
upstream auth error: SASL auth failed
```
emma: Any recent deploys to cache clients or memcached cluster?
kai: No app deploys. Infra team rotated memcached credentials 15:00 as part of scheduled rotation — but rotation should be zero-downtime. Looks like some proxies didn't pick up new creds.
infra-bot: Notified oncall: infra team assigned - @kai, @marta.
marta: Confirmed: controllers rolled new secret to memcached nodes but a subset of edge proxies still using old secret, giving AUTH failures. That's causing auth handshake delays and connection churn.
raj: That matches why gateway timeouts spike: each cache miss then triggers model request, and our model concurrency bursts cause 5xx when capacity hit.
oncall-sre: Short-term mitigation idea: enable `X-Cache-Bypass: 1` header for affected tenants to skip cache layer. We can add a header rewrite at gateway for specific customer headers.
emma: Can we do that per-tenant? Customer impacted: org_ids 345, 678, 901.
kai: Yes — I can push a config override to route those org_ids with header set. Will take ~5 min.
marta: Also rolling back memcached secret rotation to previous value on the cluster for the proxies that failed to refresh could help. But that's higher risk.
raj: For diagnostics: please capture a failing request trace ID and the gateway logs for that trace. Useful fields: `trace_id`, `upstream.cache.error`, `upstream.model.latency`.
emma: Trace id for one failing request: trace-2026-03-17-15-04-23-abc123. Logs attached in uploads.
oncall-sre: I've applied `X-Cache-Bypass` for org 345/678/901 and increased `cache.read_timeout_ms` to 300ms on gateway global override. Early signs: 504 rate dropped ~60% for those orgs. :thumbsup:
kai: Pushing fix to rotate secrets on the remaining proxies now. Will coordinate with infra to confirm all proxy instances have new secret or revert.
marta: Postmortem notes to gather: sequence (secret rotation -> partial proxies not refreshed -> auth errors -> cache timeouts -> fallback to model -> model saturation -> 5xx/504s), affected org list, mitigation steps (bypass + timeout change + secret reconcile), ETA for full remediation.
raj: For long-term: recommend rolling secret rotation via control-plane rollout that ensures proxies pick up new secret before invalidating old one (grace period), and add circuit-breaker so large spike of cache misses doesn't overwhelm model pools (throttling + queuing).
emma: Customers notified via status with initial update. I'll send follow-up once infra confirms full secret reconciliation.
kai: Secrets reconciled on remaining proxies at 15:12 UTC, memcached auth errors cleared in metrics by 15:14. Post-change observation: backend 2xx rate restored but we should monitor for 30m.
oncall-sre: Last check at 15:24 shows errors back to baseline. I'll leave the cache timeout change for 30m then revert to normal if stable.
marta: I'll open an incident postmortem with timeline and action items.
emma: Thanks all. Summary for support: root cause = partial memcached credential mismatch during rotation causing auth failures -> cache timeouts -> fallback to model -> downstream 504/502 for hosted inference customers. Mitigations = per-tenant cache bypass, increased cache timeout to reduce tail, secret reconciliation.
raj: Filing follow-up ticket to add safer rotation pattern and model-pool circuit-breaker.
emma: Closing this thread when postmortem exists. :white_check_mark:
